meta.crossing_definition: sustained: 30-day average volume reaches the threshold, not a one-day touch
meta.model_rationale: GBM on daily volume was tested and rejected: the calibration double-counted the Ito correction, and daily volatility near 0.35 compounds to a one-year dispersion that makes any crossing probability an artifact. An unconstrained AR(1) on the log 30-day average was also tested and rejected: the fitted phi of roughly 0.998 cannot be distinguished from a unit root, so its implied stationary level is an unstable extrapolation. The model is therefore a random walk with drift on the log 30-day average with bootstrapped residuals, plus a 30-day block bootstrap of daily returns as a non-parametric check.
caveats: Drift estimated from a trending window extrapolates that trend; +67%/yr (365d) and +455%/yr (180d) are not sustainable indefinitely, so long-horizon probabilities are upper bounds
A random walk cannot anticipate structural breaks, new integrations, or saturation of the current growth driver
Thresholds move with NEAR price and capture rate; they are recomputed at every run and shown in the header
Residual bootstrap preserves the empirical error distribution but assumes errors are exchangeable over time
The two windows disagree because the regime changed; the disagreement is information, not error
